title: Vue tests: behavior, timing, and contracts

drawbacks: Mocks and simulated DOM tests have limits.

trace.title: Arrange a boundary
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A pure test checks a transformation. A component test mounts a small UI and exercises its public behavior.

A browser test verifies real navigation, layout, and browser APIs. Choose the layer that can observe the defect.

Prefer accessible roles and labels when finding controls. A test that clicks .blue-button can pass while the button has no useful name.

Wait for Vue updates and promises deliberately. nextTick flushes Vue updates; flushPromises helps pending promise callbacks in tests. Neither proves a real remote service works.

Control time and request outcomes. Resolve B before A to test a race.

Return an HTTP rejection to test draft preservation. Keep a few real integration checks so mocks do not invent an API contract that the server does not provide.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Arrange the state and fake boundary → act as a user → flush the required update boundary → assert visible outcome and emitted contract.

Confirm the test fails when the repair is removed.

For focus trapping, hydration, scroll, and browser back behavior, run a real browser check. A simulated DOM does not implement all browser layout/accessibility behavior.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
Testing private implementation details makes refactors expensive. Broad snapshots may miss the important failure.

Arbitrary sleeps make the test depend on machine speed.
